types.name: AnimationSystem
types.doc:
System that updates all AnimatorComponents each frame
Samples animations, computes bone hierarchies, produces skinning matrices

Evaluation is two-phase: a serial gather pass resolves every animator's
components and LOD interval, then the per-animator evaluation (sampling,
blending, IK, motion matching, bone palette) fans out across the job system
with per-thread scratch — each job writes only its own entity's components,
so results are bit-identical to the serial order. Animation events are
queued during evaluation and their callbacks dispatched serially afterwards
in gather order, never from worker threads.

members.name: SetLODFocus
members.doc:
Update-rate LOD (EX6, UE URO analog): animators beyond a.LODNearRadius
from the focus sample every a.LODNearInterval frames (a.LODFarInterval
beyond a.LODFarRadius), banking the skipped dt so animation time stays
continuous. Scene feeds the main camera position each tick.

members.name: NoteRendered
members.doc:
UE's VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption input: the scene calls this for
every skinned animator it draws inside the camera frustum. With
a.OffscreenInterval > 0, an animator not drawn for two updates samples
at least that coarsely (dt banked). Nothing changes until a renderer
has noted something, so a headless server is never throttled.

members.name: GetBudgetDeferredCount
members.doc:
UE's AnimationBudgetAllocator: with a.BudgetMs > 0, the evaluation
pass is held to that many milliseconds by deferring the lowest-priority
animators (offscreen first, then by significance or focus distance) to
a later frame with their dt banked. An animator is never deferred more
than a.BudgetMaxDeferFrames frames in a row.

members.name: ResolveControllerAsset
members.doc:
Load the animator's authored .manim controller into `controller`, once.
Update() calls this itself, so hydration paths only need it when they
want the controller live before the first tick. A failed load is not
retried — it logs once and leaves `controller` null.

members.name: ResolveControlRigAsset
members.doc:
Load the component's authored `.mcontrolrig` into `rig`, once, off the
VFS. Update() calls this in the serial gather pass so the evaluation
fan-out only reads the loaded rig. A failed load logs once and leaves
`rig` null (the animator's pose passes through untouched).

members.name: ResolveRetargeterAsset
members.doc:
Load the component's authored `.mretarget` into `options`, once, off the
VFS. Update() calls it in the serial gather pass, so a scene, a prefab
and a runtime spawn all pick the asset up without any of them knowing it
exists. A failed load logs once and leaves the in-code options standing.

members.name: HydrateAssets
members.doc:
Every asset an animator in `world` will need — controller, montage
document, control rig, retargeter, pose assets — read now rather than
by the first Update that evaluates it, where the VFS reads ran on the
game thread inside the frame. Called when play starts; anything still
unresolved (a later spawn) falls back to the in-frame path. Returns how
many animators it touched.

members.name: HydrateEntityTree
members.signature: static uint32_t HydrateEntityTree(World& world, EntityID root)
members.doc:
The same for one spawned tree — the root and every descendant. The
sector streamer calls it per restored root inside its spawn budget, so
a streamed-in character's assets are read under that budget instead of
by the first Update that evaluates it.

members.name: IsEvalDuringPhysicsEnabled
members.doc:
a.EvalDuringPhysics: UE's parallel anim evaluation beside the physics
step. The scene arms the next Update with DeferToPhysicsStep when it
kicks the step asynchronously; that Update then evaluates only the
animators something reads before the step (root motion the character
movement consumes, morph channels the morph pass samples) and leaves the
rest. KickDuringPhysics gathers and fans those out with no wait, after
the DuringPhysics tick group so no actor tick touches an animator a
worker holds. JoinDuringPhysics waits for them before the step's
write-back moves any transform. FinishAfterPhysics then runs what needs
the stepped world — foot IK raycasts and the pose after them — and the
serial post-pass (leader copies, sync phases, events). Without a
physics overlap the scene never arms it and Update runs everything.

types.name: AnimationSystem::FRootMotionPoseSource
types.doc:
What actually produced this frame's pose, for the wrap seam. A single
clip is one entry at weight 1; a blend space is the 2 or 3 clips it
blended, with the same weights, in the same order.

The seam correction reads the pose at the clip's START and END. Taking
those from ONE representative clip while the pose itself was a blend
makes the wrap frame's root delta wrong by the difference between the
clips' root travel — small, but it accumulates over every lap, and it is
exactly the case a locomotion blend space is in for its whole life.

members.name: kMaxClips
members.doc: matches UpdateResult::bs2Clip

members.name: times
members.doc:
The (phase-matched) time each clip was sampled at, in seconds on
that clip's own timeline — what the published pose-clip
contributions carry so morph channels sample where the pose did.

members.name: Add
members.signature: void Add(const AnimationClip* clip, float weight, float timeSeconds = 0.0f)

members.name: Representative
members.doc:
The clip whose timeline the phase is expressed in — the first, which
is how SampleControllerPose picks its representative duration.

types.name: FAssetPackageObjects
types.doc:
A reflected object as a package's payload (ROADMAP §23.2): a root node
`<Class> "<Name>" { ... }` carrying the MPROPERTY values that differ from
the class's default object — a new field is absent and reads at its
default, an unknown key is skipped. This is how a data asset, a settings
object or any MCLASS type becomes an asset without a hand-written writer.

members.name: WriteObject
members.signature: static MDF::MdfNode* WriteObject(MDF::MdfPackage& package, MObject* object, const std::string& name)
members.doc:
Appends `object` to the payload and adds every asset path its values
name to the import table. The package takes the object's class when it
has none. Null when the object has no registered class.

members.name: MakeObjectPackage

members.name: ReadObject

Constructs the root's class by name and applies its properties. The

next collection. Null when the class is unknown or abstract.

members.name: ApplyObject

members.name: primaryTickGroup
members.doc:
Default is PrePhysics — flip in subclass ctor when ordering
matters.

members.name: canEverTick
members.doc:
UE's bCanEverTick: actors that opt out never enter the tick
schedule at all — the dominant case for placed scenery. Defaults ON
for compatibility; subclasses (and the Visual Script bind, which knows whether
any Tick graph or latent node exists in the chain) flip it off.

members.name: tickOnAnyThread
members.doc:
UE's bRunOnAnyThread: the world may run this actor's tick (its
tickInterval pacing, the virtual Tick and the components it ticks) on a
task-graph worker, in parallel with the group's other such actors once
their prerequisites have ticked. Off by default, and only for an actor
whose tick touches nothing but its own state — no spawning or
destroying, no structural ECS work, no Visual Scripting, no other actor's fields.
Components with a tickGroupOverride still tick on the game thread.

members.name: CustomTimeDilation
members.doc:
Per-actor multiplier on top of the world's time dilation, so a
single actor can run in slow motion (or keep full speed while the
rest of the world is slowed) without a second clock. The world
reads it when it computes this actor's tick delta; 1 = follow the
world exactly, 0 = frozen.

members.name: OnConstruct
members.doc:
Construction event (UE Construction Script analog). Runs
after the backing entity exists and before BeginPlay; the editor
re-runs it when instance properties change, so keep it
idempotent — derive state, don't accumulate it. Default: no-op.

members.name: RegisterComponents
members.doc:
Publish this actor onto its backing ECS entity. Runs at
registration — scene load included — so a placed actor draws and
inspects in the editor without beginning play. Default impl
dispatches OnRegister to every component; overrides must call
Super::RegisterComponents().

members.name: BeginPlay
members.doc:
Called once when the world begins play, or at registration for an
actor spawned into a world that already has. Default impl
dispatches BeginPlay to every component — overrides must call
Super::BeginPlay(). Gameplay startup only: the ECS mirror is
already published by RegisterComponents.

members.name: HasActorBegunPlay
members.doc:
True between the world's BeginPlay and EndPlay. MWorld owns the
flag, which is what makes double-BeginPlay across a PIE
Play/Stop/Play cycle impossible.

members.name: tickInterval
members.doc:
Tick pacing (UE TickInterval): 0 = every frame. When set, the world
accumulates this actor's dilated time and Tick fires once the
interval elapses, receiving the ACCUMULATED delta — dt-integrating
gameplay stays exact, it just steps coarser. The cost lever for
things that don't need per-frame updates (distant AI, ambience).

members.name: DispatchTick
members.doc:
Non-virtual dispatch the world calls: applies tickInterval pacing
BEFORE the virtual Tick, so subclass overrides pace with it.

members.name: TickOverrideComponents
members.doc:
World-driven pass for components whose tickGroupOverride names this
group: they tick AFTER every actor of the group, regardless of the
owner's own group. Inherit components (-1) tick inside Tick as ever.

members.name: Tick
members.doc:
Per-frame tick. Default: dispatch to every component's
TickComponent. Override on actors that need pre/post-component
logic; call Super::Tick(dt) to keep components ticking.

members.name: Destroyed
members.doc:
Fired by MWorld::Destroy right before EndPlay — the explicit-
destruction hook (UE Destroyed()). NOT called on world teardown,
play end or ejection; use EndPlay + GetEndPlayReason for those.

members.name: EndPlay
members.doc:
Called when the actor is removed from the world. Counterpart
to BeginPlay — default impl dispatches EndPlay to components
in reverse order. Overrides must call Super::EndPlay().

members.name: GetLocation
members.doc:
Transform
Root transform — typically the root MSceneComponent's transform.
Convenience accessors mirror to the root component.

members.name: GetSocketTransform
members.signature: bool GetSocketTransform(const std::string& socketName, Vec3& outLocation, Quat& outRotation) const
members.doc:
Sockets — the named attachment points a mesh carries (a muzzle, a
hand bone, a roof mount). Asks every scene component on the actor,
in attachment order, and returns the first that owns the name;
the transform comes back in WORLD space, composed onto the owning
component, which is what a caller placing an effect or spawning a
projectile actually needs. False leaves the outputs untouched.

members.name: CanMoveAtRuntime
members.doc:
False for a Static or Stationary actor once its world has begun play
(UE's mobility rule); the refused move logs a warning naming the actor.

members.name: AddComponent
members.doc:
Component management
Attach a component. Takes ownership of the raw pointer; the
actor will destroy it on EndPlay. Use the templated
CreateDefaultSubobject<T>() helper in subclass constructors.

members.name: RemoveComponent
members.doc:
Detach a component added at run time (a script component a designer
removed): it leaves the list and loses its owner; the caller ends its
play and lets it be collected. False when it was not this actor's.

members.name: CreateDefaultSubobject
members.signature: template<typename T> T* CreateDefaultSubobject(const char* name)

members.name: InitDefaultSubobjectConfig
members.doc:
The INI's MPROPERTY(Config) values from the component class's default
object: a constructor-made component is never cloned from a default,
so this is the only way a project's Game.ini reaches it.

members.name: FindComponent
members.doc:
Find first component of the given type. Returns nullptr if not
attached. O(N) in component count — fine for typical actors
with <10 components.

members.name: GetComponents
members.doc: Read-only access to the full component list (for iteration).

members.name: GetComponentByClass
GetRootComponent
members.doc:
The scene root — the component whose transform is the actor's
transform. Always an MSceneComponent. nullptr for actors that
are pure logic (controllers / managers).

members.doc: World

members.name: SetWorld
members.doc:
Out-of-line: the TObjectPtr store barrier needs the complete type,
and MWorld is only forward-declared here.

members.name: GetBackingEntity
members.doc:
ECS bridge
Backing entity in the scene's ECS World. Created by
MWorld::RegisterActor when the world has an ECS world attached;
INVALID_ENTITY otherwise (pure-logic worlds, tests). Components
mirror render/physics state onto it so the flat systems
(SceneRenderer's MeshRenderer iteration, TransformSystem) see
actors without knowing about the OO layer. MWorld::Tick syncs
the root component transform into the entity each frame.

members.name: PullFromBackingEntity
members.doc:
Adoption counterpart to the OnRegister push: seed the root transform
from the entity's TransformComponent and fan PullFromMirror out to
every component, so re-publishing the mirror reproduces the scene's
authored values instead of class defaults.

members.name: AddTag
members.doc:
Gameplay tags
Hierarchical identifiers (Damage.Physical, Faction.Enemy.Goblin)
used for AI behaviour predicates, ability requirements,
gameplay filters. HasTag uses hierarchical matching — a query
for "Damage" matches an actor tagged "Damage.Physical.Slash".

Storage is a vector of canonical dot-paths rather than a
TSet<FGameplayTag>, which is what makes the field reflectable and
therefore serialized: MHT maps std::vector<T> to PropertyType::Array
and has no set support at all, and FGameplayTag itself is not a
reflected struct (its only member is an FName, which is not a
PropertyType either). A vector of strings needs nothing new from
the header tool, round-trips through the existing scene writer and
shows up in the inspector. Uniqueness is enforced in AddTag; actors
carry a handful of tags, so the linear scan is not worth a set.

members.name: GetArchetypeName
members.doc:
The template (archetype) this instance derives its defaults from, or
empty when it derives straight from the class CDO. When set, the scene
writer diffs the instance against the named template instead of the CDO
(instance -> template -> CDO -> class), so raising a template default
reaches every instance of it that never overrode the field.

members.name: AddTickPrerequisite
members.doc:
Tick prerequisites
This actor's Tick runs only after every prerequisite in the SAME
tick group has ticked this frame; prerequisites in other groups
are already ordered by the group sequence. Cycles degrade to
registration order. Dead prerequisites are ignored and pruned.

types.name: AActor::ETickGroup
types.doc:
Tick ordering inside a frame — UE5's ETickingGroup analog.
Scene::OnUpdateRuntime dispatches in this order: PrePhysics →
DuringPhysics → [ECS system update, which is where the physics step
and TransformSystem live] → PostPhysics → PostUpdateWork. Most
gameplay defaults to PrePhysics; place logic that must observe
post-physics poses in PostPhysics or PostUpdateWork.

Mowo does not split the physics step into "step" and "resolve", so
DuringPhysics runs BEFORE the step alongside PrePhysics rather than
inside it — the useful distinction here is pre-step vs post-step.
MWorld::Tick(dt) (the convenience whole-frame path used by headless
drivers) runs all four groups back to back with no physics between
them; only the Scene path honours the ordering above.

types.name: AActor::EEndPlayReason
types.doc:
Why EndPlay is firing (UE EEndPlayReason). Overrides read it via
GetEndPlayReason() — a parameter would break every existing override.

members.name: StartMatch
members.doc:
Spawns GameState + PlayerController + default pawn, possesses,
flips match state to InProgress. Idempotent (second call no-ops).
A dedicated server sets spawnLocalPlayerOnStart false first — the
match starts with no local player and pawns arrive per connection

members.name: SetStartOverride
members.signature: static void SetStartOverride(const Vec3& location, const Quat& rotation)

instead of at an APlayerStart. One-shot — consumed by that placement
and cleared by the editor when play stops — and process-wide because
the game mode that will read it does not exist yet when the editor
decides where play begins.

members.name: PostLogin

before a departing player's controller is torn down. Override the
virtuals in a game mode subclass or bind the delegates from anywhere.

types.name: AVisualScriptActor
types.bases: public AActor, public IDamageable, public IVisualScriptHost

members.name: score
members.doc: State a Visual Script graph can read/drive (reflected)

members.name: ServerAddScore
members.doc:
RPC-annotated surface. A Visual Script graph calling these gets real routing:
the VM ships a Server call to the authority, a Client/Multicast call to
its client(s), through FNetSession — never the LG6 execute-locally trap.
Concrete bodies double as the routing fixtures the self-tests pin.

members.name: MulticastVisualScriptVars
members.doc:
Visual Script variable replication (the receive half). The authority packs every
replicated Visual Script variable that changed into this blob and multicasts it;
riding an RPC-flagged MFUNCTION is what gives the update the authority
rule for free — FVisualScriptRpcCodec refuses a Multicast that did not arrive
from the server, so a client cannot push variable state at its peers.
A variable whose value actually changed and that declares a RepNotify
runs that function afterwards, on the receiver only.

members.name: InstallVisualScriptActorFactory
members.doc:
Visual Script binding
Adopt a synthetic class + its event graphs (called by the spawn path
before BeginPlay). After this GetClass() reports `synthetic`.
Installs every backing class's factory into VisualScriptClassRegistry, keyed by
the native base it stands in for, plus the runtime's hooks. Idempotent.

members.name: TryBind
members.signature: static void TryBind(AActor* actor, MClass* cls)
members.doc:
Spawn-path helper: bind iff `actor` is visual-script-backed (any backing class)
and `cls` is a Visual Script synthetic class (cls->userData set). A no-op for
native actors/classes.

members.name: GetClass
members.doc: Report the synthetic Visual Script class when bound, else the native MClass.

members.name: Destroyed
members.doc:
Self-events, the Blueprint set a graph can implement by naming an event
graph after them. Each one is looked up in the class chain and skipped
when the class has no graph of that name:
"Destroyed"            an explicit MWorld::Destroy, before EndPlay
"AnyDamage"            TakeDamage; DamageAmount / DamageInstigator set
"OnHit"                a physics contact begins on the backing entity or
a placed slot; PinPayload = the other actor,
HitLocation / HitNormal / HitImpulse set
"InputAction.<Name>"   the named input action Started this frame
"InputAction.<Name>.Released"  ... Completed
"InputAction.<Name>.Held"      ... Triggered (every firing frame)
"OnTriggerEnter" / "OnTriggerExit"  a Trigger slot's overlaps (existing)
Input graphs are polled from Tick against the process-wide action system,
like Blueprint's Auto Receive Input: no possession needed, and a later
possession cannot wipe them the way a MPlayerInput binding would be.

members.name: TakeDamage

members.doc:

members.name: CollectVarOverrides
members.doc:
Every variable whose current value differs from the class-declared
default: the Visual Script analog of a CDO delta. Runtime-only keys (PinPayload)

authored variables round-trip through the scene.

members.name: IsAuthoredOverride
members.signature: static bool IsAuthoredOverride(const VisualScriptValue& current, const VisualScriptValue* seeded)
members.doc:

instance state, or is it still the class default `seeded` handed this
instance? Only the first survives a class-default edit — the second has
to follow the new default, which is what makes raising a default in the
Actor Editor reach every placed instance that never touched the field.
`seeded` is null when the class did not declare the variable at bind
time, and a value nobody ever seeded is authored by definition.

members.name: PushReplicatedVars
members.doc:
Ship every replicated variable whose value differs from what this actor
last got onto the wire. Authority-only — a remote instance returns false
without touching the net layer. `forceFull` re-sends the whole set (a
peer that just joined has none of it). Returns true when an update
actually left. Public so a headless test can drive one update without a
frame loop.

Rewrites an `Actor` node written at `storedVersion` into the shape the
class has now — a renamed key, a split field, a changed unit — before
any property is read.

members.name: RegisterClassVersion
members.signature: static void RegisterClassVersion(const std::string& className, uint32_t version, FMigrateFn migrate)
members.doc:
An actor class's own data version, the counterpart of a component's
TypeDescriptor version + migrate. The writer stamps `_version` on the
Actor node when it is above 1; the reader migrates an older node in
place and counts a newer one, which stops the level from being saved
over by a build that could not read it. Unregistered classes are
version 1. Registration is by the class's current name; a renamed class
keeps its version through the Type redirect.

members.signature: static bool WriteActor(AActor* actor, MDF::MdfNode& entityNode)
members.doc:
Write `actor` as an `Actor` child of `entityNode`. No-op returning

type cannot be respawned by name, so persisting it would silently
lose it on load).

members.name: ReadActor
members.signature: static AActor* ReadActor(MWorld& world, EntityID backingEntity, MDF::MdfNode& entityNode)
members.doc:
Respawn the actor described by `entityNode`'s `Actor` child into
`world`, adopting `backingEntity` instead of creating a fresh one.
Property values are applied BEFORE BeginPlay so component mirrors
publish the restored state onto the entity. Returns nullptr when
there is no `Actor` child or the class is no longer registered.

members.name: ResolveActorReferences
members.signature: static void ResolveActorReferences(MWorld& world, AActor* actor, const MDF::MdfNode& entityNode)
members.doc:
Re-applies the actor references in `entityNode` once every actor they
can name exists. ReadActor already resolves the ones it can; a loader
that spawns a batch calls this per actor afterwards so an edge to an
actor later in the file is not lost. Idempotent.

members.name: CopyFromArchetype
members.signature: static void CopyFromArchetype(MObject* archetype, MObject* target)
members.doc:
Copy every supported MPROPERTY value from `archetype` onto
`target`, up the whole class chain — the same kinds the writer saves,
references only when they name another placed actor. This is what
makes spawn a CDO clone rather than a bare construct().

members.name: CloneActorFromArchetype
members.signature: static void CloneActorFromArchetype(AActor* archetype, AActor* target)
members.doc:
Overlay a whole actor: CopyFromArchetype for the actor itself plus
each of its same-named / same-class components. Both the CDO-clone
spawn path and template (archetype) instancing route through here.

members.name: WriteObjectProperties
members.signature: static void WriteObjectProperties(MObject* object, MDF::MdfNode& node)
members.doc:
The property half of the actor format for an MObject that is not an
actor — MSaveGame. Every supported MPROPERTY up the class chain is
written as a property of `node`, the FULL set rather than a delta
against the CDO: a save records what the player had, and a patch that
raises a class default must not rewrite it.

members.name: ReadObjectProperties
members.signature: static void ReadObjectProperties(MObject* object, const MDF::MdfNode& node)

members.name: WriteObjectDelta
members.signature: static void WriteObjectDelta(MObject* object, MDF::MdfNode& node)
members.doc:
The asset form: only what differs from the class's default object, so
a raised class default reaches every asset that never overrode it — the
opposite choice from a save. A class with no CDO writes the full set.

members.name: RemapActorReferences
members.signature: static void RemapActorReferences(MDF::MdfNode& entityNode, const std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string>& uuidRemap)
members.doc:
The world-state journal's half: an `ActorState` child of `entityNode`
carrying the actor's and its named components' MPROPERTY(SaveGame)
fields and, for a Visual Script actor, the value of every declared variable —
full values, not a delta, because the overlay lands on the authored
level. Without it a placed actor's state (an opened door, a looted
chest, any Visual Script variable) reverted on every sector reload and every
save. False, and nothing written, when there is nothing to keep.
A pasted or duplicated set gets fresh entity uuids; its actor references
still named the originals, so a copied door pointed at the original's
switch instead of the copied one. Rewrites every "actor:<uuid>" and
"component:<uuid>/<name>" under `entityNode`'s Actor node whose uuid is
a key of `uuidRemap` (old uuid string -> new); references outside the
set keep naming what they named.

members.name: ExtractUnknownActorKeys
members.signature: static bool ExtractUnknownActorKeys(AActor* actor, const MDF::MdfNode& entityNode, MDF::MdfNode& outCarried)
members.doc:
Keys in `entityNode`'s Actor node that `actor`'s class has no field for
— written by a build that has the field — into `outCarried` (an `Actor`
node with `Properties` and per-component `Component` children). The
loader keeps them only for a document stamped by this engine or a newer
one (FContentVersionStamp::CarriesUnknownKeys), and the writer merges
them back under what it wrote, so a colleague on the older build no
longer strips the newer build's actor fields by saving the level. A
class with a Custom field is not carried: its handler's own keys are
indistinguishable from unknown ones.

types.name: ESnapshotRefScope
types.doc:
Where a captured object reference pointed, in terms that survive the
destroy/respawn: an address does not, but "the component of this actor
named X" and "the actor named Y of class Z" both do.

members.name: Unresolvable
members.doc:
Live at capture but neither an actor, one of the holder's components,
nor the world — nothing to look it up by, so it restores as null.

members.name: strings
members.doc:
AActor::m_tags is a std::vector<std::string>; without a container slot
here every actor lost its gameplay tags on a game-module reload.

members.name: objects
members.doc:
One entry for a single object reference, one per element for a vector
of them.

members.name: elementSize
members.doc:
Set for a vector of fixed-width elements: `raw` is elementCount blocks
of elementSize bytes. The element size is re-checked against the
reloaded property row, so a widened element type skips instead of
shredding the array.

members.name: backingEntity
members.doc:
Backing ECS entity at capture time. Zero (INVALID_ENTITY) for the
destroy/respawn hot-reload path, which matches actors by class and
name; set by CaptureActorState for the in-place PIE path, which matches
the SAME actor instance back up by this stable id.

types.name: FActorSnapshotUtils
types.doc:
In-place PIE state preservation — the pre-Play snapshot the editor takes
so Stop can undo Play WITHOUT destroying and recreating the world.

CaptureActorState keeps every filtered actor ALIVE and records its backing
entity alongside its property values. RestoreActorStateInPlace finds each
actor back by that entity and writes the values onto the SAME instance,
then re-publishes the ECS mirror — so actor and entity identity are stable
across a Play/Stop cycle. Actors spawned during Play (no matching capture)
are left for the caller to reap. Returns the number of actors restored.

members.doc:
Anchors the fixed clock at anchorPhase01 of the representative clip's
cycle. Call again whenever the composition's clip identities change (a
state switch, a montage taking over) so the clock re-anchors on the
pose's own time instead of running on from the previous clip's.

members.signature: bool MatchesSource(const FSourceClip* clips, uint32_t count) const

Same clip identities in the same order; weights are allowed to differ
(a blend space slides them every frame without changing the cycle).

members.name: FixedStep
members.signature: void FixedStep(float stepSeconds, Vec3& outDeltaPosition, Quat& outDeltaRotation)
members.doc:
One fixed step: advance the clock by stepSeconds (play rate already
applied) and return the root delta over exactly that interval, in the
root bone's local space. A loop seam inside the step is split so the
wrap loses nothing; a step longer than the cycle folds whole cycles in.

members.name: PeekStep
members.signature: void PeekStep(float stepSeconds, Vec3& outDeltaPosition, Quat& outDeltaRotation) const

members.name: AdvanceFrame
members.signature: FFrameResult AdvanceFrame(float frameDt, float fixedDt, float bankedSeconds, uint32_t maxSteps, float playRate)
members.doc:
The frame driver: runs the steps the physics loop will run this frame
(mirroring its accumulator) and returns the published delta.

members.name: StepsForFrame
members.signature: static uint32_t StepsForFrame(float bankedSeconds, float frameDt, float fixedDt, uint32_t maxSteps)
members.doc:
How many fixed steps PhysicsSystem::Update runs for a frame of frameDt
with bankedSeconds already in its accumulator, including its catch-up
cap. The arithmetic is the physics loop's own, in the same order, so
the two agree at every float boundary.

types.name: FCharacterRootMotionStepper::FSourceClip
types.doc:
One clip of the composition the pose was built from, at the weight the
pose blend used. Blend-space clips are sampled phase-matched, so the
stepper's clock is a phase and the representative clip gives it a length
in seconds.

members.name: publishedDelta
members.doc:
What to hand the per-frame consumer. CharacterMovementSystem divides
the published delta by the FRAME dt and the physics loop integrates
that velocity over the fixed steps it runs this frame, so this is
pre-scaled by frameDt / (steps * fixedDt): the capsule ends the frame
having moved exactly steppedDelta. On a frame that runs no step it is
the coming step's velocity, so readers of the capsule velocity see no
zero-frame flicker.

members.name: steppedDelta
members.doc: The exact displacement the fixed steps of this frame add up to.

members.name: deltaRotation
members.doc:
The root yaw across those steps. The consumer applies rotation once
per frame directly, not through physics, so it is not rescaled.

members.name: health
members.doc: snapshot. These are the CURRENT (aggregated) attribute values.

members.name: statusFlags
members.doc:
Discrete status word — bit 0 = dead, higher bits = game-defined status
flags. Rides the reliable channel so a dropped snapshot never strands a
client on a stale death/status.

members.name: grantedAbilities
members.doc:
Every ability the server has granted, as wire ids
(MAbilitySystemComponent::AbilityWireId — FNV-1a32 of the tag path, the
same id the activation RPCs carry). A client uses it to refuse an
activation the server would reject anyway, saving the round trip.

members.name: cooldownAbilities
members.doc:
Live cooldowns as two INDEX-ALIGNED arrays: ids and the seconds left on
each. Two arrays rather than one array of pairs because the codec takes
fixed-width ELEMENTS — a struct entry needs a per-element codec, and a
uint64 (id<<32 | ms) is not in the replicable type set either. Readers
must walk min(size, size): a lost or reordered update must not read one
array past the other.

members.name: CooldownFor
members.doc:
Seconds left on `wireId`, 0 when it is not on cooldown. The pairing
invariant is enforced HERE so every caller gets it right.

members.name: lastRequestedAbility
members.doc: Runtime-only bookkeeping (not replicated as fields — driven by the RPCs).

members.name: lastCueId
members.doc:
Last replicated cue, kept for observers and tests. The cue itself is
dispatched the moment the RPC lands, not buffered — cues are cosmetic
and a frame of queueing buys nothing, while a queue would need a policy
for what to drop when several arrive in one tick.

members.name: ServerActivateAbility
members.doc:
Client → server: "the owning client wants to activate ability N, and it
has already predicted the result under prediction key K." MFUNCTION(Server)
auto-installs an OwnerOnly policy, so only the peer that owns the pawn may
send it. The server validates + activates on the real ASC and answers the
owning client with a confirm or a reject carrying the same key, so the
client reconciles the exact activation it predicted.

members.name: MulticastAbilityActivated
members.doc:
Server → every client: "ability N activated." Runs on the server and on
each ghost, so cosmetic reactions (cues, montages) can play everywhere.

members.name: ClientConfirmAbility
members.doc:
Server → owning client: the predicted activation stands. The client drops
the retained baseline; the replicated attributes converge the values.

members.name: ClientRejectAbility
members.doc:
Server → owning client: the predicted activation was refused. The client
rolls its ASC back to the captured baseline for that key.

members.name: MulticastGameplayCue
members.signature: void MulticastGameplayCue(uint32_t cueId, uint32_t cueEvent, Vec3 location, float magnitude)
members.doc:
Server → every client: "this cosmetic cue fired." Reliable, because a
dropped death cue leaves a corpse with no effect on it and nothing later
repairs it — a cue is an edge, not a state a snapshot can re-converge.

The tag travels as FGameplayCueDispatcher::CueWireId (FNV-1a32 of the
path); a receiver that has never named that tag cannot resolve it, so the
cue is counted in cuesUnresolved and dropped rather than guessed at. The
location rides along because a cue plays in the WORLD, not on the owner:
an impact effect belongs at the hit, not at the actor's pivot.

Sky-light gain across the cycle. Applied to a SkyLightComponent on
the same entity; the night floor keeps a moonlit scene readable instead

members.doc: Down (default — floor decals)

members.name: YPositive

types.name: DecalProjectorComponent
types.doc: ECS component for deferred decal projectors

members.name: material
members.doc: Decal material (albedo, normal, metallic-roughness textures)

members.name: materialPath
members.doc: VFS/relative path for serialization round-trip

members.name: projection
members.doc: Projection direction (which axis/direction the decal projects along)

members.name: size
members.doc:
Projection volume, in metres, as the box's FULL extent along each local
axis (the projector mesh is a unit cube spanning -0.5..0.5, scaled by
this on top of the entity transform). The projection axis component is
the depth the decal reaches into geometry, half of it on each side of
the entity's origin.

members.name: fadeFactor
members.doc: Blending

members.name: angleFadeStart
members.doc: cos(angle) where fade begins (1.0 = facing camera)

members.name: angleFadeEnd
members.doc: cos(angle) where fully transparent

members.name: drawOrder
members.doc: Sorting priority (lower = rendered first)

members.name: affectsBaseColor
members.doc: Per-channel GBuffer write control (packed into DecalAffectFlag bits at submit)

members.name: layerMask
members.doc:
Which camera layer masks this decal is visible to. A view whose culling
mask shares no bit with this one skips the decal entirely — the same
relationship an entity's layer has with the camera, expressed as a mask
so one decal can be limited to, say, the gameplay view but not a
security-camera view.

members.name: lifetime
members.doc:
Lifetime in seconds; 0 means the decal never expires (an authored floor
marking). Anything a shooter sprays at runtime — bullet holes, scorch
marks, blood — wants a finite one, because the alternative is an
unbounded pile of draw calls over a long match.

members.name: fadeOutTime
members.doc:
Seconds of fade at the end of the lifetime. The decal's opacity ramps to
zero over this window instead of popping out of existence.

members.name: age
members.doc: Seconds since the decal was placed, advanced by DecalSystem.

members.name: expired
members.doc:
Set when the lifetime runs out. The owning entity is destroyed by
DecalSystem on the following tick; the pool watches this to reclaim
slots it handed out.

members.name: GetEffectiveFade
members.doc:
Opacity multiplier for the current age: fadeFactor until the fade window
opens, then a linear ramp to zero.

types.name: ExponentialHeightFogComponent
types.doc:
UE5's ExponentialHeightFog: distance fog whose density falls off
exponentially with height. Density and falloff use UE's authoring scale
(density 0.02 thins to a third over a kilometre at the fog height), and the
in-scattering colour follows the sky when the scene has an atmosphere.

members.name: fogHeightOffset
members.doc:
World height the density is authored at. The actor's own height is added,
so moving the actor moves the fog.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

members.name: hingeOffset
members.doc: Local offset from the entity origin to the hinge line (the door edge).

members.name: impulseThreshold
members.doc:
Normal impulse (kg m/s) a hit must deliver to damage the breakable. It
used to compare contact speed, which let a light pebble thrown hard break
what a heavy crate settling onto it could not.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FogVolumeComponent
types.doc:
A local volumetric-fog volume. The froxel fog pass injects this volume's
density (scaled by its albedo/emissive) into the light grid wherever a froxel
falls inside it, on top of the global height fog — so a room fills with haze
or a sphere of coloured smoke sits in the world without affecting the whole
level. Box uses the entity transform's scale as half-extents; Sphere uses the
radius. Reflected so the Details panel edits every field with zero editor
code.

members.name: density
members.doc: Scattering density (extinction) inside the volume. Higher = thicker.

members.name: albedo
members.doc:
Single-scattering albedo — the tint the volume gives to light passing
through it (1,1,1 = neutral grey haze).

members.name: emissive
members.doc: Constant emissive radiance added inside the volume (glowing fog).

members.name: edgeFeather
members.doc:
Fraction of the extent spent fading the density to zero at the boundary
so a volume blends into the surrounding air instead of a hard edge.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

members.name: layerIndex
members.doc:
0-3 read the first weightmap plane, 4-7 the second. The range used to
stop at 3 because only one plane was ever sampled, which silently made
half the palette ungrassable.

members.name: alignToSlope
members.doc:
0 = every clump stands straight up, 1 = every clump lies in the surface
plane. Vertical grass on a hillside reads as cardboard standing on edge;
fully aligned grass on a cliff hangs out of it. The blend is what an
artist actually tunes.

members.name: renderBatches
members.doc:
GPU-instanced render batches — built by
FoliageSystem when r.Foliage.GPU != 0 (grass clump instances + tree
impostor cards), submitted per frame by Scene::OnRender. Never
serialized; a scene load rebuilds them through the fingerprint.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FFoliageType
types.doc:
One row of the painted-foliage palette — UE5's UFoliageType, kept on the
scene instead of as an asset: a type only means something together with the
instances painted with it, and a scene that loses either half is broken.

members.name: meshPath
members.doc:
Empty draws the component's blade clump, so a fresh palette row grows
something before anyone imports a plant.

members.name: density
members.doc:
Instances per square metre the brush fills toward. A dab counts what is
already under it and adds only the difference, so holding the brush still
saturates instead of stacking.

members.name: radius
members.doc:
The closest two instances of this type may stand (UE's Radius): a
candidate inside it of one already placed is dropped, so trees keep
their crowns apart however long the brush is held. 0 = no spacing.

members.name: scaling
members.doc:
UE's Scaling: 0 Uniform (every axis takes the Min/Max Scale roll, which
is Scale X), 1 Free (X, Y and Z roll apart), 2 Lock XY (the ground axes
share the X roll, Z rolls apart). Y and Z are UE's axes: Y across the
ground, Z up.

members.name: alignToNormal
members.doc:
0 = stands on world up, 1 = stands on the surface normal, blended in
between; the same control the terrain palette carries.

members.name: alignMaxAngle
members.doc:
UE's Align Max Angle: an instance aligned to its surface tilts at most
this far from world up. 0 = no limit.

members.name: cullDistance
members.doc: 0 = never culled by distance.

types.name: FoliageInstancesComponent
types.doc:
Hand-painted foliage: the palette and every instance the Foliage viewport
mode placed with it. UE5's AInstancedFoliageActor. Instances are stored in
WORLD space inside one packed field (see FFoliageInstanceCodec) rather than
as a reflected array — ten thousand rows is not a details-panel property,
and the scene format stays one string key that an older loader simply
leaves alone.

members.name: instances
members.doc:
FFoliageInstanceCodec blob. Hidden from Details: the Foliage mode is the
editor for it, and a wall of base64 is not an editable row.

members.name: revision
members.doc:
Bumped by every edit the tool makes. The build fingerprint reads it
instead of hashing the blob, so a 100 000-instance field costs nothing
per frame to watch; undo restores an older number, which differs from the
built one exactly when the blob does.

members.name: bladeWidth
members.doc: The clump drawn for palette rows with no mesh.

members.name: renderBatches
members.doc:
GPU-instanced clump batches, one per palette row that qualifies, built
by FoliageSystem and submitted by Scene::OnRender the same way the
terrain field's are. A dense paint used to cost one submesh submit per
clump; a batch is one indirect draw for the whole row.

types.name: FootstepComponent
types.doc:
Footstep audio driven by the surface under the character's feet.

Cues are found by convention rather than through a mapping table: the cue
for a surface is "<cueFolder>/<SurfaceType>.cuegraph", with "Default.cuegraph" as
the fallback. A designer adds gravel footsteps by dropping Gravel.cuegraph in
the folder — no registry to keep in sync, and a surface with no cue simply
stays silent instead of playing the wrong thing.

members.name: strideDistance
members.doc: Metres of horizontal travel between steps at a normal walk.

members.name: lastSurface
members.doc:
Observable result of the last step — what it decided the ground was and
which cue that resolved to. Gameplay, debug overlays and the self-test
all read these.

types.name: HairStrandsComponent
types.doc:
A strand groom (.mhair guide curves) on a character. Put it on the entity
with the skeletal mesh: the guides ride the named bone of that mesh's posed
skeleton (or the entity itself when the bone is empty or missing),
simulate at runtime, and are interpolated into camera-facing ribbons drawn
into the G-buffer with Marschner-lite shading. Reflected, so the Details
panel edits every field with zero editor code.

members.name: attachBone
members.doc:
The skeleton bone the groom is authored relative to (a head, say); the
guide points are in that bone's space. Empty = the entity's space.

members.name: roughness
members.doc: Longitudinal width of the Marschner lobes: low = a tight, glossy sheen.

members.name: widthScale
members.doc: Multiplies the groom's root and tip widths.

members.name: strandsPerGuide
members.doc: Render strands interpolated per guide; 0 keeps the groom's own count.

members.name: stiffness
members.doc: Pull toward the rest shape per step (root; a third of it at the tip).

types.name: IKGoal
types.doc:
A single IK constraint on a three-bone chain.

Lifetime model:
- Author at edit time: chain bone indices + pole hint. These typically
point at a character's left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg.
- Drive at runtime: targetPosition (and optionally targetRotation) is
pushed each frame by gameplay code or the foot-IK pass — the
AnimationSystem applies the solve before computing global transforms.

One IKComponent owns N goals; the typical biped uses 2-4 (hands + feet).

members.name: name
members.doc: editor label, e.g. "LeftFoot"

members.name: chain
members.doc: root/mid/end + pole + weight

members.name: hasTargetRotation
members.doc: false => end bone follows chain freely

members.name: autoFootRaycast
members.doc:
Auto foot-IK (system-driven by raycast each frame)
When `autoFootRaycast` is true the AnimationSystem performs a
downward raycast from the end bone's current world position before
running the solver. On hit: targetPosition is updated to hit.point +
hit.normal * groundOffset, and (if alignToNormal) targetRotation is
rebuilt to align the foot's up-axis to the surface normal. On miss:
the goal weight is zeroed for this frame so the limb falls back to
the animated pose smoothly. Targets remain in *world space* for
these goals; the IK pass converts to skeleton-local before solving.

members.name: raycastUp
members.doc: ray start: bone world pos + up*raycastUp

members.name: raycastDistance
members.doc: max ray length from start downward

members.name: groundOffset
members.doc: foot height above hit point

members.name: alignToNormal
members.doc: overrides targetRotation each tick

members.name: raycastLayerMask
members.doc:
Player (layer 2) is cleared, matching CameraControllerComponent. The ray
starts `raycastUp` above the ankle, which is inside the character's own
capsule — and a character now carries a real body in the collision world,
so an all-layers mask planted every foot on the capsule's bottom cap
instead of the floor.

members.name: footIkAuthoredWeight
members.doc:
Runtime weight state for auto foot-IK. The authored chain weight is
captured once so a raycast miss can ease the runtime weight to zero and
a later hit can ease it back to the AUTHORED value — the old code wrote
a hard 0/1, destroying the authored weight and popping on transitions.

members.name: lockPlantedFoot
members.doc:
Foot locking (UE foot placement's plant lock). While the animated foot
moves slower than `plantSpeed` (m/s, world) it is planted: the IK
target stays on the spot where it planted, so turning on the spot or
a speed mismatch between clip and movement no longer slides the foot.
The lock lets go once the animated foot drifts `unlockDistance` (m)
away or lifts off, and the target eases from the locked spot to the
live one over `unlockBlendTime` seconds.

members.name: footLocked
members.doc: Runtime lock state.

types.name: FABRIKGoal
types.doc:
FABRIK goal — N-bone chain (>2 bones), iterative position-only solver.

Unlike `IKGoal` (which is hard-tied to the analytical 3-bone solver),
FABRIK works for chains of any length: spines, tails, tentacles, fingers.
Pole hint here applies a swing around the root→end axis after the
position pass, so it's an orientation control over the *middle* joints
only, not a strict bend-plane constraint like the 2-bone solver.

Targets are author-space (model-space relative to the entity transform),
same convention as `IKGoal::targetPosition` for non-foot-IK goals.

members.name: goals
members.doc: 2-bone (arms, legs)

members.name: fabrikGoals
members.doc: N-bone (spine, tail, fingers)

members.name: fullBody
members.doc:
Whole-body solve (UE's Full Body IK): several effectors negotiating over
the joints they share, instead of N chains where the last one to run
wins the spine. There is ONE per component because it is a statement
about the whole body — two full-body setups on one character would be
two answers to the same question. Empty `effectors` = off, so an existing
IK component is unchanged.

It runs BEFORE the two-bone and FABRIK goals: this places the body, and
foot IK is the fine ground contact that has to be the thing that lands
last, or a whole-body reach lifts the feet back off the floor.

members.name: pelvisBone
members.doc:
Pelvis adjustment for auto foot-IK. Without it, a character standing
across a step has one leg solved onto the lower surface by stretching it
to its limit — the classic straight-locked leg and hyperextended knee.
The fix is the one every AAA foot-IK does: drop the whole body by the
DEEPEST correction any foot needs, then let each leg's solve place its
own foot from there, so no leg has to reach further than the animation
already had it reaching.

Off until a pelvis bone is named, so an existing IK setup is unchanged.

members.name: pelvisMaxDrop
members.doc:
Cap on the drop, in world units. A bad raycast (a hole in the level, a
trigger volume the mask forgot) would otherwise sink the character.

members.name: pelvisAllowLift
members.doc:
Also lift the body when every foot is ABOVE its animated height (walking
up onto a kerb). Off by default: lifting is the half that most often
reads as floating when the ground data is noisy.

members.name: pelvisOffset
members.doc: Runtime: the eased offset currently applied, in world units along up.

types.name: ELipSyncMode
types.doc:
How the mouth is driven: by the level of the entity's own audio source
(jaw opens with loudness), by the text of what is being said (visemes
paced over the clip), or both layered.

types.name: LipSyncComponent
types.doc:
Lip-sync over morph targets. Sits next to a Morph component and the
entity's AudioSource: while the source plays, the jaw target follows the
signal's envelope and, in Text mode, one of five viseme targets is held
for each letter of the line, paced over the clip's length. Target names
are looked up on the mesh's morph targets; a name the mesh does not carry
is skipped, so a head with only a jaw still talks.

members.name: jawTarget
members.doc:
Amplitude: envelope RMS × Gain, clamped, smoothed at Response per
second.

members.name: text
members.doc: Text: the line spoken. Empty takes the caption of the playing cue.

members.name: visemeStrength
members.doc: Weight a held viseme reaches, and how fast visemes cross-fade.

members.name: jawIndex
members.doc:
Headless fallback: with no mesh to look names up on, these indices
into the Morph weights are used directly (-1 = by name only).

types.doc: ECS component for materials

members.doc: (this component's, or the asset's), never the owner itself.

members.name: ownedMaterial
members.doc:
Strong reference to an inline (non-asset) material. Shared with the
entity's MeshRendererComponent, so the two components hold ONE object and
the last one to die frees it — with its GPU texture refs, exactly once.
Null when `material` views an asset-owned material: the asset holds
that Ref, and a reimport keeps the object in place.

members.doc:
Take ownership of an inline material and point the view at it. The view
is set FROM the Ref: adopting a raw pointer into the Ref would let a
second owner meet the first on one object.

members.doc:
UUID of the MaterialAsset (invalid for inline materials).
Used for serialization round-trip through the Asset system.

members.doc: Asset reference (non-empty when loaded from asset pipeline)

members.doc: Convenience accessors (delegate to material if available)

members.doc:
Target indices the animation wrote LAST frame. They reset to zero before
each accumulation so a channel that exists only in a clip the blend has
left decays to zero instead of freezing at its last sampled value.

types.name: NavMeshLinkComponent
types.doc:
Off-mesh connection — a manual traversal link between two points on
the nav mesh. Agents take it when its endpoints are on the planned
route; useful for jumps, teleports, ladders, drop-down ledges, doors
that aren't on the same polygon island.

Endpoints are stored in world space (set them via the editor gizmo
or from script: agent.SetDestination on the other side will route
through the link automatically once it's part of the baked nav mesh).

Lifecycle: links are baked INTO the dtNavMesh — they're not runtime
dynamic. Add the component, re-bake, and the connection appears in
pathfinding. To change a link, edit it and re-bake.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: NavMeshModifierComponent
types.doc:
Per-entity nav-mesh area override. Attach to an entity that also has a
MeshRenderer to tag every triangle that mesh contributes to the bake
with a custom area type.

Area types follow Unity's NavMeshModifier convention:
0  = Walkable (default — same as having no modifier)
1  = Water        (walkable but agents may path around it via filter cost)
2  = Ladder
3..62 = user-defined
63 = Not Walkable (the mesh is cut OUT of the bake — useful for fences,
glass walls, "fake floor" decals that shouldn't be paths).

dtQueryFilter::setAreaCost lets agents weight different areas — e.g.
AI that "avoids water unless necessary". The default cost is 1.0; a
water tile with cost 2.0 makes the planner prefer dry routes.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: ENavObstacleShape
types.doc:
Runtime obstacle that re-cuts the nav mesh through dtTileCache. Place
on an entity (closed door, fallen tree, deployable barricade) — the
system removes its volume from agents' walkable surface within a
frame or two, and restores it when the component is disabled or
destroyed.

Two shapes:
Cylinder — `radius` and `height`. Cheap; matches doors / pillars
well. Footprint is a disc, centred on the entity's
TransformComponent.position.
Box      — `halfExtents` axis-aligned. Tighter fit for crates and
furniture but slightly more expensive to evaluate.

Obstacles only affect tiles inside an EXISTING baked nav mesh — they
don't extend the mesh's bounds. Designers want the scene baked once,
then drop obstacles at gameplay time.

types.name: PlanarReflectionComponent
types.doc:
A mirror plane: the scene re-rendered from the camera MIRRORED about this
entity's plane, sampled by surfaces lying on it.

Why this exists next to SSR and ray-traced reflections. SSR can only reflect
what is already on screen, so a mirror shows nothing of what stands behind
the camera — the one thing a mirror is for. RT reflections solve that but
need hardware ray tracing and cost a trace per pixel. A planar reflection
re-renders the scene ONCE per mirror and is exact for a flat surface, which
is why every engine keeps it for floors, water and actual mirrors.

The plane is the entity's local XZ plane: origin at its world position,
normal along its world UP. Rotate the entity to tilt the mirror.

members.name: extent
members.doc:
Half-size of the reflecting rectangle in the plane. Pixels outside it
keep whatever SSR/probe reflection they had — the mirror has an edge,
and beyond it there is no mirror to reflect in.

members.name: thickness
members.doc:
How far off the plane a pixel may sit and still count as ON it. Depth
precision and a mirror's own thickness both put the visible surface a
little off the mathematical plane; too tight and the mirror flickers,
too loose and the wall behind it starts reflecting.

members.name: resolution
members.doc:
Capture resolution. A planar reflection is re-rendered every frame, so
this is the knob that decides what it costs.

types.name: ProceduralLookAt
types.doc:
One runtime look-at goal. The AnimationSystem runs it after IK, before the
final FK, aiming `constraint.bone`'s forward axis at `targetPosition`. Set
`targetInWorldSpace` when gameplay supplies a world target (the common case
of looking at another actor) — the system converts it into model space via
the entity transform before solving.

types.name: ProceduralSpringChain
types.doc:
One spring-bone chain plus its persistent dynamic state. The state carries
tip positions/velocities across frames; the solver (re)initializes it from
the animated pose on first use.

types.name: ProceduralAnimComponent
types.doc:
Secondary/procedural motion for a skeletal actor — look-at aiming and
spring-bone chains (ponytails, tails, cloth straps). Attach it next to an
AnimatorComponent; the AnimationSystem applies both after IK so they layer
on the final animated pose.

types.name: ProjectileMovementComponent
types.doc:
UE's ProjectileMovementComponent: kinematic flight for anything thrown,
fired or launched, without a rigid body. FGameplayMovementSystem integrates
the velocity each frame, sweeps the step so a fast projectile cannot tunnel
through a wall between frames, and bounces or stops on what it hits. The
weapon ProjectileComponent is a different thing — damage and explosions for
the Combat plugin — and the two can sit on one entity.

members.name: maxSpeed
members.doc:
0 = no limit. Clamps gravity and homing too, so a homing missile turns
rather than accelerating forever.

members.name: launchDirection
members.doc:
Launch direction in the entity's own space, rotated by its rotation at
the first simulated frame. The engine's forward is -Z.

members.name: collisionRadius
members.doc: Radius of the swept sphere; 0 sweeps a ray.

members.name: bounciness
members.doc: Share of the speed along the hit normal kept after a bounce.

members.name: friction
members.doc: Share of the speed along the surface lost on a bounce.

members.name: bounceStopSpeed
members.doc:
Below this speed after a bounce the projectile comes to rest instead
of chattering on the floor forever.

types.name: RetargetComponent
types.doc:
Retargets the animator's clips — authored against `sourceSkeleton` — onto
the entity's own (target) skeleton at runtime. When enabled and a source
skeleton is set, the AnimationSystem samples the active clip against the
source rig, then replays it onto the target through an FRetargetMap so a
character can reuse animation authored for a differently-proportioned rig
with matching bone names. `map`/`built` are the runtime cache — the map is
rebuilt whenever the source or target skeleton changes.

members.name: retargeterPath
members.doc:
Authored .mretarget asset holding the name map, prefix strips and
per-bone translation modes for this SOURCE→TARGET rig pair. Resolved
once by the AnimationSystem into `options` below, so every hydration
path (scene load, prefab, spawn) picks it up without the caller knowing
the asset exists — the same shape as AnimatorComponent::controllerPath.

members.name: options
members.doc:
Name-remap rules + per-bone translation modes fed to the map build.
Loading a retargeter asset overwrites this wholesale, so code that sets
it by hand must not also name an asset.
After mutating, clear `built` so the next evaluation rebuilds.

types.name: RollbackPlayerComponent
types.doc:
The entity a rollback player drives: each simulated frame the session
writes that player's input here (confirmed or predicted) before the
rollback steps run, and a rollback rewinds it with the rest of the world.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: RotatingMovementComponent
types.doc:
UE's RotatingMovementComponent: spins the entity at a fixed rate — pickups,
fans, turbines, a radar dish — with no graph ticking it. A pivot offset
swings the entity around a point instead of its own origin.

members.name: rotationRate
members.doc: Degrees per second about X (pitch), Y (yaw) and Z (roll).

members.name: pivotTranslation
members.doc:
The point the entity swings around, in its own space. Zero spins it in
place.

members.name: rotationInLocalSpace
members.doc:
On: the rate is applied about the entity's own axes (a tumbling
asteroid). Off: about the parent's axes (a turntable stays level).

types.name: SceneCaptureComponent
types.doc:
UE's SceneCaptureComponent2D: a camera that renders the world into a
RenderTargetAsset instead of the screen — a security monitor, a portal, a
rear-view mirror, a minimap. The entity's transform is the camera and looks
down its own -Z, the axis CameraComponent looks down; the target names an `.mrt`
asset whose image any material's Texture Sample can bind. Each capture is
a full scene render through its own SceneRenderer view, so every-frame
captures cost what they say; a one-shot capture (captureEveryFrame off)
renders once when it first appears and again on RequestCapture.

members.name: captureEveryFrame
members.doc:
Off = capture once on the first frame the component is seen, then only
when captureRequested is raised (a Visual Script graph or C++ calling for a
fresh frame). On = a full render every frame.

members.name: captureRequested
members.doc:
Raised to force a capture next frame whatever captureEveryFrame says;
the capture system clears it.

members.name: viewId
members.doc:
The renderer view this capture renders through (0 = none yet), sized
to the target; recreated when the target's size changes.

types.name: SkyAtmosphereComponent
types.doc:
UE5's SkyAtmosphere: the physical atmosphere the sky, the sky light capture,
aerial perspective and the sun's colour are all computed from. Coefficients
are authored the UE way, as a colour times a scale per kilometre; the
defaults are Earth.

types.name: SpringArmComponent
types.doc:
UE's SpringArmComponent: holds its CHILD entities at the end of an arm that
trails behind the entity, pulls in when the world is in the way, and can lag
behind the motion it follows. Parent a camera entity (or a light, a mesh) to
the arm and it rides the end. FGameplayMovementSystem runs it after physics,
so the arm reads the pose the frame settled on.

members.name: targetOffset
members.doc:
Offset of the arm's start from the entity, in world space (a shoulder
height above a character's origin).

members.name: socketOffset
members.doc:
Offset of the end from the arm's tip, in the entity's own space (an
over-the-shoulder shift to the right).

members.name: probeSize
members.doc: Radius kept clear around the end — the lens never clips a wall.

members.name: cameraLagSpeed

members.name: endLocation

Where the end sits this frame, in world space, and how long the arm
actually is after collision.

types.name: StreamableComponent
types.doc:
World-partition opt-in (UE's "Is Spatially Loaded"). Entities
carrying this marker are bucketed into streaming sectors by the
editor's Build Streaming Sectors pass and spawned/despawned at
runtime by FSectorEntityStreamer as the camera crosses sector radii.
Persistent world furniture (cameras, sun, managers) simply doesn't
carry the component and always stays loaded.

members.name: layer
members.doc:
Data layer (UE Data Layers analog). Empty = the base layer,
always spawned with its sector. Named layers spawn only while
StreamingManager::SetLayerActive(name, true) holds — toggling a
layer live spawns/despawns its fragments in already-resident
sectors.

members.name: grid
members.doc:
Runtime grid (UE World Partition's runtime grids). Empty = the default
grid. A named grid is declared in the level's sector manifest with its
own cell size, optional cell height and radii; one the manifest does not
declare yet is added with the default grid's cell size.

types.name: StreamingSourceComponent
types.doc:
A point the world streams around (UE's WorldPartitionStreamingSourceComponent).
Streaming used to follow the main camera alone, which is wrong the moment a
world has more than one viewer: on a listen server the sectors around every
remote player were non-resident on the host, so their physics, their
interactables and the geometry they stood on simply were not there. Every
entity carrying this component is a source, and a sector's distance is its
distance to the NEAREST one — the camera included.

FNetSession puts one on every player pawn it spawns, so co-op is correct
without anyone authoring it; place it by hand on anything else that must
keep the world around it loaded (a vehicle a player left running, a camera
about to cut, an AI the designer wants simulated).

members.name: radiusScale
members.doc:
Scales the three streaming radii for this source alone. Below 1 a source
keeps less around it than the camera does — the setting for a distant
co-op player on a memory-bound machine, where the alternative is every
player paying the camera's full footprint.

types.name: FTerrainSplinePoint
types.doc:
A control point of a landscape spline. `position.y` is the target height the
corridor is graded to, in the same terrain-local meters the heightfield uses.

members.name: tangent
members.doc:
Explicit outgoing tangent, in the same terrain-local meters. Zero means
"derive it" and the centreline stays the Catmull-Rom the numeric-only
authoring produced — the viewport's tangent handles are the only thing
that writes a non-zero value, so old data reads back unchanged.

types.name: FTerrainGrassType
types.doc:
A grass type authored on the TERRAIN's layer palette rather than as a
sibling FoliageComponent. UE5 hangs a grass type off the landscape layer
info, and for the same reason: "sand does not grow grass" is a property of
the painted layer, not of some other component that happens to be attached to
the same actor. One entry per (layer, plant) pair; several may share a layer.

members.name: alignToSlope
members.doc:
0 = every instance stands straight up, 1 = every instance lies in the
surface plane. Grass on a hillside that stays vertical reads as a decal
standing on edge; a bush that fully aligns on a cliff hangs sideways off
it. The blend is the control an artist actually wants.

members.name: editLayersPath
members.doc:
The non-destructive sculpt stack, stored beside the terrain exactly like
the weightmaps are: the heightmap file holds the FLATTENED result, this
holds base + per-layer deltas, and a load recomposites from it so hiding
a layer still restores what was underneath. Empty = the terrain was saved
flattened and sculpting writes straight into the base.

members.name: retopoPath
members.doc:
The retopologize XZ offset grid, stored the same way and for the same
reason as the edit-layer blob: it describes where the render samples sit,
which the flattened heightmap beside it cannot express.

members.name: layer0Surface
members.doc:
A terrain is not one material. Each painted layer carries its own
surface, and the collider resolves per square from the dominant weight,
so walking off grass onto the rock you painted changes the footstep.

members.name: splinePoints
members.doc:
Splines are deliberately absent from the rebuild fingerprint: applying
one is an explicit command that writes into the edit session, so a
fingerprint rebuild triggered by moving a point would discard the sculpt
the previous apply produced.

members.name: grassTypes
members.doc:
Grass authored on the layer palette. Empty is the historical behaviour:
scatter comes from a sibling FoliageComponent, or from nothing.

members.name: streamingTile
members.doc:
One tile of a tiled import. A tile streams: TerrainSystem builds its
mesh, quadtree and collider when the camera comes within the streaming
load radius and releases them past the unload radius. Off for a
stand-alone landscape, which is always resident.

members.name: streamingAlwaysLoaded
members.doc:
Never evicted regardless of distance — the tile holding the player start,
or one a scripted sequence needs standing.

members.name: weightmapRevision
members.doc:
Bumped by every weightmap write. Layer-gated foliage scatters from those
weights, so painting grass onto a slope has to re-scatter it — and the
only other signal available was the terrain's own build fingerprint,
which would rebuild every chunk and the collider for one brush dab.

types.name: VdbVolumeComponent
types.doc:
A sparse volume from a NanoVDB file — smoke, fire, a cloud — ray-marched
over the lit scene after the volumetric fog (FVdbVolume, the VDB pass). The
grid sits in the entity's space: its voxel coordinates map to world through
the file's own voxel size and origin, then through the entity transform.
Reflected, so the Details panel edits every field with zero editor code.

members.name: vdbPath
members.doc:
An uncompressed .nvdb file (NanoVDB; nanovdb_convert turns an OpenVDB
.vdb into one).

members.name: densityGrid
members.doc:
Grid names to read. A missing density grid falls to the file's first
fog-volume grid; a missing temperature grid means no emission.

members.name: densityScale
members.doc: Extinction per unit of stored density per world unit. Higher = thicker.

members.name: albedo
members.doc: Single-scattering albedo: the tint light picks up passing through.

members.name: anisotropy
members.doc:
Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy: > 0 scatters forward (bright rim when
looking toward the sun), 0 is isotropic.

members.name: temperatureScale
members.doc:
Stored temperature x this = Kelvin. 1 for grids already in Kelvin; the
default reads a normalised 0..2 grid as up to 2000 K.

members.name: emissionStrength
members.doc: Blackbody emission multiplier; 0 turns the fire off and leaves the smoke.

members.name: maxResolution
members.doc:
Longest axis of the dense brick the grid is resampled into. Higher keeps
finer wisps and costs memory (4 bytes a voxel).

types.name: WaterZoneComponent
types.doc:
A water zone: the authored object that says which stretch of world the water
system is responsible for. UE's WaterZone does three jobs and so does this
one — it bounds which bodies participate, it fixes the water info texture's
extent and resolution (instead of the extent being whatever the union of the
bodies happened to be, which moved every time a body was edited), and it
carries the far-distance mesh that fills the horizon past the bodies
themselves.

A scene with no zone still works: the info texture falls back to the union of
the published bodies and nothing draws a far mesh. A zone is how you take
control of that, not a thing you must have.

members.name: extent
members.doc:
Square side, in metres, centred on the entity. Bodies whose extent does
not reach inside it are left out of the info texture entirely.

members.name: infoResolution
members.doc:
Info texture resolution per side. Fixed by the zone rather than by the
cvar so a designer can pay for a narrow river's channel without raising
the cost of every other scene.

members.name: farDistanceMesh
members.doc:
The horizon filler: a coarse quadtree surface out to Far Distance Extent,
drawn under everything else so an ocean does not simply stop where its
body's extent runs out.

members.name: color
members.doc:
Shading of the far surface. Deliberately its own set rather than borrowed
from a body: the far mesh has no bathymetry and no shoreline, and matching
it to a lake's tint is an authoring choice, not a rule.

types.name: FEngineModularRegistry
types.doc:
The engine-wide seam a plugin's InitializeModule hook writes into so its
systems and asset serializers join the running engine without any core
edit. Scene consults the registered systems alongside its built-in table;
every host applies the registered serializers after its built-in set.
Reflected components need nothing here — they self-register through the
generated MHT statics the moment the plugin DLL loads.

members.name: RegisterSceneSystem
members.doc:
Forwarders into the ECS-level FSceneSystemRegistry (E3.1 NO1) —
kept here so plugins keep one registry to talk to.

members.name: SceneSystemRevision
members.doc:
Bumped whenever the system set changes so Scene can rebuild its cached
tick order instead of missing a plugin that loaded after the first tick.

members.name: IsCharacterInputCaptured
members.doc:
True while ANY extension's mode owns the shared mouse buttons —
used by the template's built-in binds and by other extensions'
binds alike, so modes stand down for each other symmetrically.

members.name: SerializerFactory
members.doc:
Plain function pointer, NOT std::function: the factory crosses the
plugin DLL boundary and lives in a vector the registry reallocates —
relocating a std::function built by another image crashed the
packaged game (each image owns its allocator; same rule as the
FModularSceneSystem hooks above).

members.name: RemoveAllInModule
members.doc:
Drops every fragment, character extension and serializer factory whose
function pointers live inside the given module image — after the DLL
frees they are calls into unmapped pages (SaveGame walks fragments,
SetupPlayerInput walks extensions, every host replays the factories).
Scene systems are swept by FSceneSystemRegistry itself. Driven by the
FModuleManager unload broadcast. Returns the number of entries dropped.

members.name: ApplyRegisteredSerializers
members.signature: template<typename TManager> void ApplyRegisteredSerializers(TManager& manager) const
members.doc:
Called by each host right after it registers its built-in serializers.
Templated so it works with either concrete manager (Editor/Runtime)
without a base-class virtual.

types.name: FEngineModularRegistry::FStateFragment
types.doc:
Save/travel-carried world state as data: a system that owns durable
gameplay state (quest log, faction standings) registers a fragment;
SaveGame writes every fragment with state into the save root and
FTravelManager carries them across a level change — neither names a
concrete system type, so the owner can live in a plugin. `Name` is
the MDF node type (e.g. "QuestState") and must stay stable: it is
the on-disk save format. Plain function pointers for the same ABI
reason as FModularSceneSystem.

`Version` is stamped on the fragment's node as `schema_version`. A node
from an older build goes through `Migrate` (node, its version) before
`Deserialize`; one from a newer build is skipped and logged, because the
reader would misread a layout it has never seen. Absent on disk = 1.

types.name: FEngineModularRegistry::FCharacterExtension
types.doc:
Template-character gameplay extensions: a plugin that adds a
character-driven mode (base building was the first) registers input
binding + a per-frame camera aim feed instead of the template naming
its system. Plain function pointers (ABI rule above). BindInput runs
after the template's built-in binds during SetupPlayerInput; OnAimRay
gets the camera rig's world-space ray once per possessed-character
frame.

members.signature: void (*OnAimRay)(ACharacter&, const Vec3& origin, const Vec3& direction) = nullptr

members.doc:

the template's combat binds stand down (build mode was the first:

module (its vtable is in that image): the purge marks such an actor
pending-kill, and a template left pointing at it would hand the next
spawn freed memory.

types.name: FFeetAnchoredBody
types.doc:
The placeholder body of anything whose origin is its feet: a character
controller (its Jolt capsule is lifted by half its height), a nav agent
(Detour writes the navmesh surface point into its position). The built-in
"capsule" and "cylinder" primitives are centred on their origin and two
metres tall, so drawn as they are such a body stood half underground at the
wrong size. FitAll rebuilds them at the body's radius and height with their
base on the origin every frame the size changed, and lifts any other
primitive so its lowest point rests on the feet. Mesh assets keep their own
pivot: an imported character (the mannequin) is authored feet-down already.

and captureless, the FAISignals rule. An entity reported twice keeps the
last size, and the built-in source runs last.

members.name: PushAttributesToNetState
members.doc:

members.name: PullAttributesFromNetState

members.name: PredictActivation
members.doc:
Client-side prediction
On the owning client: predict the activation on the local ASC now
(cost/cooldown/cue land this frame) and stamp the request the client will
send the server with the returned prediction key. Returns 0 when the local
CanActivate check failed — nothing predicted, no request to send. Fill
net.lastRequestedAbility / net.lastRequestedPredictionKey from the return
and route ServerActivateAbility with them.

members.name: RequestAbilityActivation
members.doc:
The one-call client entry point: predict locally, then route the
request — over the wire when this process is a connected client,
straight into the authority mailbox otherwise (offline / listen
local player). Returns the prediction key (0 = CanActivate failed,
nothing predicted, nothing sent).

members.name: AbilityWireId
members.doc:

members.name: ExecuteGameplayCue
members.signature: void ExecuteGameplayCue(FGameplayTag cueTag, EGameplayCueEvent event, float magnitude = 0.0f, const Vec3& location = Vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), MObject* instigator = nullptr)
members.doc:
Fire a cosmetic cue EVERYWHERE. On the authority it plays locally and
fans out to every ghost through MulticastGameplayCue; off the authority
it does nothing at all, because the server's multicast is what will play
it — firing here too would double it on the client that asked.

For a cue a client should play IMMEDIATELY as part of a prediction (the
muzzle flash on the ability it just predicted), use
ExecuteLocalGameplayCue: local only, never replicated, so the incoming
multicast is the ghosts' copy and not a second one for the predictor.

members.name: OnRegister
members.doc:
Lifecycle — AActor dispatches.

OnRegister publishes the component's ECS mirror. It runs when the
actor joins a world, which is scene load in the editor — a placed
actor is therefore visible and inspectable without playing. Put
everything that only describes the actor here: it must be safe to
run in the editor, must not spawn actors, and must not start
anything that ticks.

BeginPlay runs when the world begins play (PIE Play, or the first
MWorld::Tick on a headless driver) and once per actor. Put gameplay
startup here — playing audio, spawning a camera rig, seeding runtime
state from config.

members.name: PullFromMirror
members.signature: virtual void PullFromMirror(World* ecs, EntityID entity)
members.doc:
Inverse of the OnRegister push, run when an actor adopts an entity the
scene loader already populated: read exactly the mirrored fields the
push writes, before serialized actor deltas apply.

members.name: RefreshMirror
members.doc:
Re-publish the fields a component mirrors onto the ECS (its light, mesh,
audio, ...). Each mirroring component overrides it; the base has nothing
to push. Virtual so a writer that only knows the component — a script's
property setter — can refresh what the renderer reads after a raw write.
