Grades the component's spline corridor into the heightfield and, when
`spline_layer` is set, paints that layer along it.

members.name: EnsureEditLayers
members.doc:
Edit layers. Created lazily around the current editable field; the field
stays the composite everything downstream reads.

members.name: SaveEditLayers
members.signature: bool SaveEditLayers(EntityID entity, const std::string& absPath)
members.doc:
Edit-layer persistence. Save writes base + every delta plane to an
absolute path; the caller then points the component's `edit_layers_path`
at the matching VFS path so the scene records it. Load replaces the live
stack and recomposites, so the field the renderer and the collider read
still equals base + visible layers. EnsureEditLayers loads the
component's path once per path change, which is what makes a reopened
scene non-destructive again without an explicit editor action.

members.name: LoadEditLayers

members.name: FlushEditsForScene
members.doc:
Writes every dirty edit-layer stack and retopo offset grid beside the
scene file and points each component at what it wrote, so a plain
"save the level" keeps the terrain non-destructive without the artist
remembering to press Save Stack. `scenePath` is the VFS path the scene
itself is written to; the blobs land next to it as
"<scene stem>_Terrain<entity>.mtel" / ".mtro". Returns how many files
were written. The manual Save / Reload buttons stay: an explicit save is
still what you want after an experiment you do NOT intend to keep.

members.name: EnsureOffsets
members.doc:
Retopologize. The heightfield is never rewritten — the offset grid says
where each of its samples SITS, so the surface is unchanged and only the
tessellation slides along it.

texture on first use. Called from the retopo ops themselves — the same
produce-phase seam the weightmap upload uses, because recording GPU work
from a World update would land it in the wrong command buffer.

members.name: BuildNavGeometry
members.signature: bool BuildNavGeometry(EntityID entity, uint32_t resolution, std::vector<Vec3>& outVertices, std::vector<int32_t>& outIndices) const
members.doc:
Hole-aware navigation geometry: a triangle soup in ENTITY-LOCAL meters
at `resolution` samples per side, with every square whose weightmap
texel sums to nothing left out. The nav bake walks MeshRenderers for its
snapshot and the CDLOD terrain contributes no CPU mesh, so terrain is
absent from the navmesh entirely; this is the source that closes it, and
it skips holes by construction rather than by a post-pass.

members.name: TickTileStreaming
members.signature: uint32_t TickTileStreaming(const Vec3& cameraPos, const StreamingSettings& settings)
members.doc:
Tile streaming. Tiles spawned by the tiled importer carry
`streaming_tile`; this classifies them against the camera using the same
three radii the sector streamer uses and builds or releases the ones
whose residency changed, at most `settings.maxConcurrentLoads` per call.
Returns how many tiles changed state.

takes. Exposed so a caller can plan without applying.

types.doc:
Landscape ops
What one op did, so a caller can report cost and drive undo without
re-deriving the touched window.

types.name: TerrainSystem::FTerrainOffsetPacket
types.doc:
The RG16F payload the CDLOD vertex path samples, beside the R32F height
texture: one half PAIR per texel (x then z) in terrain-local METERS,
row-major over `region`. The shader adds the pair straight onto the
sample's local XZ and re-samples the height at the displaced position, so
any other unit silently rescales the whole tessellation — which is why
this is a pure static a headless row can assert without a device.

types.name: ETerrainTileState
types.doc:
Residency of one landscape tile. Deliberately NOT StreamingSector's state
machine: a sector's cost is asset IO, so it has a Loading state to wait in.
A terrain tile's cost is a synchronous CPU rebuild — mesh, quadtree bounds,
Jolt heightfield — so a tile is either built or it is not, and the budget
exists to spread those rebuilds over frames rather than to track IO.

members.name: center
members.doc:
Tile centre in WORLD space (the tiled importer spaces actors exactly one
tile apart, so this is the actor's transform translation).

members.name: alwaysLoaded
members.doc:
A tile the author never wants evicted — the one holding the player start,
a scripted set piece. Mirrors StreamingSector::alwaysLoaded.

members.name: toLoad
members.doc: Nearest first, already truncated to the frame's budget.

types.name: FTerrainTileStreaming
types.doc:
The tile half of world partition, sharing StreamingManager's policy rather
than inventing a second one: the same three radii (load < keepAlive <
unload), the same "closer is sooner" priority, the same per-frame budget. A
second streamer with its own radii would mean a tile popping in while the
props standing on it are still unloaded, or the reverse.

Decide() is a pure function of (tiles, camera, settings, budget) so the whole
policy is measurable headlessly — the residency it describes is applied by
TerrainSystem, which is the only part that needs a device.

members.name: DistanceToTile
members.signature: static float DistanceToTile(const FTerrainTileDesc& tile, const Vec3& cameraPos)
members.doc:
Distance from the camera to the tile's nearest point, in meters, on the
XZ plane. Tile EDGE, not centre: a 4 km tile whose centre is 2 km away
can still be under the camera's feet, and centre distance would evict the
ground it is standing on.

members.name: Priority
members.signature: static float Priority(const FTerrainTileDesc& tile, const Vec3& cameraPos)
members.doc:
Higher loads sooner. Negated distance, so the sort matches
StreamingManager's exactly; an alwaysLoaded tile reports distance 0.

members.name: Decide
members.signature: static FTerrainStreamingPlan Decide(const std::vector<FTerrainTileDesc>& tiles, const Vec3& cameraPos, const StreamingSettings& settings, uint32_t inFlightLoads)
members.doc:
`inFlightLoads` is how many rebuilds the caller already has queued this
frame; the plan's toLoad never exceeds settings.maxConcurrentLoads minus
that, which is what keeps a camera teleport from rebuilding forty tiles
in one frame.

types.name: WaterBodySystem
types.doc:
Builds and shades spline-driven water bodies (Ocean / Lake / River). Runs
alongside the global WaterSystem: each WaterBodyComponent gets its own
surface mesh regenerated when the spline changes, its own water material,
and a published surface descriptor the buoyancy / underwater / character
water paths query per body.

members.name: InvalidateSpectrumCache
members.doc:
Drops the parsed .mwaves cache so the next tick re-reads every spectrum
from disk. The editor calls it after saving one — without it a body keeps
the waves it was built with and the asset editor looks broken.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FWaterCarveDebounce
types.doc:
Decides when an automatic terrain re-carve should follow a spline edit.

A carve rewrites a heightfield region, refits collision and pushes an undo
record, so running one per dragged frame is both a stall and an undo stack a
designer cannot walk back through. Running one only on a button is the state
this shipped in, where the river and its bed silently disagree until someone
remembers. The middle is a debounce: every edit re-arms the timer, and the
carve runs once the edits stop.

It is a pure decision — no clock of its own, no terrain, no transaction — so
the rule is testable headlessly and the panel that owns the carve keeps
owning it.

members.name: kDefaultDelaySeconds
members.doc:
Seconds of quiet after the last edit before the carve runs. Long enough
that releasing a handle to grab the next one is still one edit, short
enough that the bed follows the water while the designer is still looking
at it.

members.name: Touch
members.doc:
An edit landed. Re-arms the timer whether or not one was already pending —
a drag is hundreds of these and must produce one carve at the end, not one
per frame.

members.name: Consume
members.doc:
True exactly once per settled burst of edits. Consuming the pending flag
here rather than leaving it to the caller is deliberate: a caller that
forgot to clear it would re-carve every frame forever, which is the
failure this class exists to prevent.

members.name: Cancel
members.doc:
Drops a pending carve without running it — the body was deleted, the tool
was disarmed, or the edit it belonged to was undone.

headers.doc: Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.

types.name: FWaterQuadNode
types.doc:
One selected leaf of the water quadtree, in the body's LOCAL space. `level`
counts down from the root: 0 is the whole ocean as one node, `maxLevels` is
the finest.

members.name: rootSize
members.doc:
Full side length of the root node, in metres, and its centre in body
space. The root is snapped to the leaf grid before selection so a camera
walking across the ocean does not shift every vertex by a sub-texel
amount each frame — that shimmer is what a camera-following mesh is
otherwise guaranteed to produce.

members.name: lodScale
members.doc:
A node subdivides while the viewer is closer than `size * lodScale`. 2.0
puts the level boundary at two node-widths, which is the range over which
the halved triangle size is not visible.

members.name: quadsPerNode
members.doc:
Quads per side inside one leaf. Every leaf carries the same count, so the
triangle budget is `selectedNodes * quadsPerNode^2 * 2`.

members.name: morphFraction
members.doc:
Fraction of a node's LOD range spent morphing its odd vertices onto the
even ones. Below this fraction the node is un-morphed; at the far end it
is fully collapsed onto the parent's sampling, so the level change costs
nothing visible. 0 disables morphing.

members.name: cullHalfExtent
members.doc:
Half-extent of the frustum-free cull box in body space. A node whose
square lies entirely outside is dropped; 0 keeps everything, which is
what a test that only measures selection wants.

types.name: FWaterQuadTree
types.doc:
A camera-following quadtree over one ocean body: the frustum's worth of the
surface is meshed finely and the rest coarsely, so a 4 km ocean costs what is
on screen rather than what exists. UE's WaterQuadTree has the same shape;
lakes and rivers keep their spline meshes, because a closed polygon and a
ribbon are not grids and gain nothing from a quadtree.

Everything here is pure geometry over a viewer position — no world, no
renderer — so the selection a camera produces is a headless test.

members.name: SelectNodes
members.signature: static void SelectNodes(const FWaterQuadTreeParams& params, const Vec2& viewLocalXZ, std::vector<FWaterQuadNode>& outNodes)
members.doc:
Depth-first selection, deterministic in node order. A node subdivides
while the viewer is inside `size * lodScale` of its square and the level
budget allows; the leaves it returns tile the root exactly.

members.name: DistanceToNode
members.signature: static float DistanceToNode(const FWaterQuadNode& node, const Vec2& viewLocalXZ)
members.doc:
Distance from a node's square to a point, 0 inside. The selection rule
and the morph factor both measure with this, so a vertex never morphs
against a distance its own node did not subdivide against.

members.name: MorphFactor
members.signature: static float MorphFactor(const FWaterQuadTreeParams& params, const FWaterQuadNode& node, const Vec2& viewLocalXZ)
members.doc:
0 = keep this level's own sampling, 1 = fully collapsed onto the parent's.
Rises across the far end of the node's LOD range.

members.name: BuildMesh
members.signature: static FWaterSplineMesh BuildMesh(const FWaterQuadTreeParams& params, const std::vector<FWaterQuadNode>& nodes, const Vec2& viewLocalXZ)
members.doc:
Meshes the selected nodes into one buffer. Vertices are welded per node
only — neighbouring nodes of the same level share an edge exactly, and a
level boundary is sealed by the morph rather than by a stitch strip,
which is the whole point of morphing.

members.name: SnapCenter
members.signature: static Vec2 SnapCenter(const FWaterQuadTreeParams& params, const Vec2& viewLocalXZ)
members.doc:
Root centre snapped to the finest leaf's vertex spacing. Exposed because
the rebuild trigger compares against it: the mesh is only worth rebuilding
when the snapped centre actually moved.

members.name: LeafVertexStep
members.doc: Vertex spacing of the finest level, in metres.

types.name: FWaterCarveTexel
types.doc:
One heightfield texel the carve wants to move, and how far it commits.
weight 1 = the channel floor exactly, 0 = leave the terrain alone; the band
between is the bank slope.

types.name: FWaterCarveRequest
types.doc:
The texel window the carve touches, half-open, plus the edits inside it. The
window is what a terrain rebuild and an undo snapshot are keyed on, which is
why it is produced even when the edit list is short.

types.name: FWaterCarveTerrain
types.doc:
How a heightfield maps to the world. The carve is written against this
rather than against the terrain module's own types on purpose: the terrain
edit API is being reworked in parallel, and a spline-to-texel solve that
takes four numbers can be tested headlessly and re-pointed at whatever the
apply side ends up being called.

members.name: originX
members.doc: World XZ of texel (0, 0) and the world size the whole field spans.

members.name: BuildRiverCarve
members.signature: static FWaterCarveRequest BuildRiverCarve(const std::vector<FWaterSplinePoint>& points, int32_t segmentsPerSpan, const Vec3& bodyOrigin, const FWaterCarveTerrain& terrain, float bankWidth)
members.doc:
Cuts the river's channel into the heightfield: the bed sits at the
spline's surface height minus its authored depth, and the banks ramp back
to the untouched terrain over bankWidth metres beyond the water's edge.
Nothing is applied — the caller decides how to blend and when to rebuild.
